root_cause: The CHG-4821 configuration change reduced the API database connection-pool maximum from 40 to 8, leaving insufficient connection capacity for the request load. The database itself remained healthy and reported available capacity.
causal_chain: CHG-4821 reduced db_pool_max from 40 to 8, with no application code changes included.
The smaller pool reached 8 active connections, while 146 requests accumulated in the wait queue.
Requests waited for database connections, causing API latency to rise and catalog requests to time out.
Rolling db_pool_max back to 40 cleared the queue and restored the error rate and latency.

event_timeline.action: Applied CHG-4821, reducing db_pool_max from 40 to 8; no application code changes were included.
event_timeline.outcome: The configuration change preceded the rise in database pool waits.

event_timeline.action: Monitoring detected increased API latency and database pool wait time.
event_timeline.outcome: Catalog API p95 latency rose from 180 ms to 4.8 s.

event_timeline.action: Responders reviewed request errors and database health checks.
event_timeline.outcome: 31% of catalog requests were timing out while database health checks continued to pass.

event_timeline.action: Responders checked API connection-pool metrics and database capacity.
event_timeline.outcome: All 8 configured connections were active with 146 requests waiting; the database reported available capacity.

event_timeline.action: Rolled back db_pool_max to 40.
event_timeline.outcome: The pool began accepting waiting requests.

event_timeline.action: Checked pool metrics, request error rate, and API latency.
event_timeline.outcome: The wait queue cleared, errors fell below 0.5%, and p95 latency reached 210 ms.

event_timeline.action: Ran API health checks and catalog search tests.
event_timeline.outcome: Both checks passed and the incident was resolved.

recovery_summary: Responders rolled db_pool_max back to 40, then verified that the connection wait queue cleared, the request error rate fell below 0.5%, p95 latency returned to 210 ms, and API health checks and catalog search tests passed.
observed_symptoms: Catalog API p95 latency increased from 180 ms to 4.8 s.
The connection pool reached 8/8 active connections with 146 requests waiting.
raw_incident_logs: 2025-04-16 09:02 UTC | Change record CHG-4821 applied to the catalog API; configuration diff shows db_pool_max changed from 40 to 8; no application code changes included. | 2025-04-16 09:04 UTC | API request p95 increased from 180 ms to 4.8 s; database pool wait time began rising. | 2025-04-16 09:06 UTC | Incident declared; 31% of catalog requests timing out; database health checks passing. | 2025-04-16 09:08 UTC | Pool metrics show 8/8 connections active and 146 requests waiting; database reports available capacity. | 2025-04-16 09:11 UTC | On-call rolled back the db_pool_max setting to 40. | 2025-04-16 09:14 UTC | Pool wait queue cleared; request error rate returned below 0.5% and p95 latency fell to 210 ms. | 2025-04-16 09:20 UTC | Incident resolved after API health checks and catalog search tests passed.
diagnostic_reasoning: The configuration diff identifies the pool-size reduction immediately before the incident. Pool metrics then show every configured connection active and a large request wait queue, while database health checks pass and the database reports available capacity. These observations identify API-side connection capacity as the cause rather than a database outage. The wait queue cleared and service metrics recovered after the pool limit was restored, supporting the diagnosis.

root_cause: CFG-771 increased message retention from 72 hours to 14 days, causing retained segments to consume the broker storage allocation. Once storage reached 100%, the broker rejected producer requests.
causal_chain: CFG-771 increased message retention from 72 hours to 14 days.
The longer retention period increased retained-segment volume and broker storage utilization.
Broker storage reached 100%, so producer requests failed with storage-quota-exceeded responses.
Failed publishes reduced order-event publish success and contributed to increasing consumer lag.
Restoring 72-hour retention and cleaning up segments reduced storage use and restored publishing.

event_timeline.action: Applied CFG-771, increasing message retention from 72 hours to 14 days.
event_timeline.outcome: The broker retained messages for a longer period.

event_timeline.action: Monitoring checked broker storage and retained-segment volume.
event_timeline.outcome: Storage utilization reached 92% as retained-segment volume increased; consumer processing remained steady.

event_timeline.action: Broker continued accepting producer requests until its storage allocation was exhausted.
event_timeline.outcome: Storage reached 100%, and producer requests began failing with storage-quota-exceeded responses.

event_timeline.action: Responders checked publish success and consumer lag.
event_timeline.outcome: Order-event publish success fell to 54%, and consumer lag began increasing.

event_timeline.action: Responders inspected broker storage and node health.
event_timeline.outcome: Retained segments consumed the allocation; broker nodes remained online and consumers continued processing.

event_timeline.action: Restored retention to 72 hours and initiated segment cleanup.
event_timeline.outcome: Broker storage utilization began to fall.

event_timeline.action: Checked storage utilization, producer requests, and consumer lag.
event_timeline.outcome: Storage fell to 76%, producer requests succeeded, and consumer lag stopped increasing.

event_timeline.action: Verified publish success and consumer lag against normal levels.
event_timeline.outcome: Publish success returned to 99.9% and consumer lag returned to its normal range.

recovery_summary: Responders restored message retention to 72 hours and initiated segment cleanup. They verified storage utilization fell to 76%, producer requests succeeded, order-event publish success returned to 99.9%, and consumer lag returned to its normal range.
observed_symptoms: Producer requests failed with storage-quota-exceeded responses.
Consumer lag increased while retained-segment volume grew.
raw_incident_logs: 2025-06-23 14:10 UTC | Broker configuration change CFG-771 changed message retention from 72 hours to 14 days. | 2025-06-24 08:40 UTC | Broker storage utilization reached 92%; retained-segment volume increased, while consumer processing rate remained steady. | 2025-06-24 09:05 UTC | Broker storage reached 100%; producer requests began failing with storage-quota-exceeded responses. | 2025-06-24 09:08 UTC | Incident declared; order-event publish success fell to 54%, and consumer lag began increasing. | 2025-06-24 09:14 UTC | Broker inspection showed retained segments consuming the storage allocation; broker nodes remained online and consumer processing continued. | 2025-06-24 09:22 UTC | Responders restored retention to 72 hours and initiated segment cleanup. | 2025-06-24 09:31 UTC | Storage utilization fell to 76%; producer requests succeeded and consumer lag stopped increasing. | 2025-06-24 09:48 UTC | Order-event publish success returned to 99.9%; consumer lag returned to its normal range; incident resolved.
diagnostic_reasoning: The incident logs show the retention change preceding the rise in retained-segment volume and storage utilization. At the time of impact, storage was at 100% and producer requests returned storage-quota-exceeded responses, while broker nodes remained online and consumers continued processing. This distinguishes storage exhaustion from a broker-node outage. Restoring the prior retention setting and cleaning up segments reduced utilization to 76%, after which producer success and consumer lag recovered.

root_cause: The settlement workers' client certificate expired at 2025-05-08 11:00 UTC, causing the clearing gateway to reject their TLS connections.
causal_chain: The worker client certificate reached the end of its validity at 11:00 UTC.
The clearing gateway rejected subsequent worker TLS handshakes with a certificate-expired error.
Settlement workers could not submit jobs, reducing job success and increasing the retry queue.
Installing the renewed certificate and restarting workers restored successful handshakes and job processing.

event_timeline.action: Settlement workers attempted TLS connections to the clearing gateway.
event_timeline.outcome: Connections failed because the gateway rejected the expired client certificate.

event_timeline.action: Monitoring checked settlement job completion and retry-queue volume.
event_timeline.outcome: Job success fell from 99.8% to 12%, and failed jobs entered the retry queue.

event_timeline.action: Responders compared the network probe with worker connection errors.
event_timeline.outcome: The gateway network health check passed, but worker TLS connections still failed with a certificate-expired error.

event_timeline.action: Operations checked certificate inventory and gateway change records.
event_timeline.outcome: The worker certificate validity ended at 11:00 UTC, and no gateway-side certificate change was recorded.

event_timeline.action: Installed the renewed worker client certificate and restarted settlement workers.
event_timeline.outcome: Workers re-established connections to the gateway.

event_timeline.action: Verified TLS handshakes, job success rate, and retry-queue drain.
event_timeline.outcome: Handshakes succeeded, job success rose to 99.7%, and the retry queue began draining.

event_timeline.action: Checked retry-queue depth and settlement reconciliation results.
event_timeline.outcome: Queue depth returned to normal and reconciliation checks passed.

recovery_summary: Operations installed the renewed worker client certificate and restarted the settlement workers. TLS handshakes succeeded, settlement job success returned to 99.7%, the retry queue drained to normal depth, and reconciliation checks passed.
observed_symptoms: Settlement worker TLS connections to the clearing gateway failed.
Settlement job success rate fell from 99.8% to 12%.
Failed settlement jobs accumulated in the retry queue.
raw_incident_logs: 2025-05-08 11:02 UTC | Settlement worker logs show TLS handshake failures to the clearing gateway: client certificate rejected because it expired at 2025-05-08 11:00 UTC. | 2025-05-08 11:04 UTC | Settlement job success rate fell from 99.8% to 12%; failed jobs entered the retry queue. | 2025-05-08 11:07 UTC | Incident declared; gateway health check from the network probe passed, while worker connections continued to fail with the certificate-expired error. | 2025-05-08 11:12 UTC | Certificate inventory confirms the worker certificate validity ended at 11:00 UTC; no gateway-side certificate change was recorded. | 2025-05-08 11:18 UTC | Operations installed the renewed worker client certificate and restarted the settlement workers. | 2025-05-08 11:21 UTC | TLS handshakes succeeded; settlement job success rate rose to 99.7%; retry queue began draining. | 2025-05-08 11:35 UTC | Retry queue returned to normal depth and reconciliation checks passed; incident resolved.
diagnostic_reasoning: The worker logs explicitly report that the client certificate was rejected because it had expired, and the certificate inventory confirms its validity ended at 11:00 UTC. The network probe to the gateway passed, and no gateway-side certificate change was recorded, so the evidence points to the worker certificate rather than a network or gateway outage. After the renewed certificate was installed, TLS handshakes and job completion recovered, confirming the diagnosis.
